summary: The I/II/III contrast is not interchangeable: I takes the thing becoming clean as its sole participant; II mnaḏ̣- and III manḏ̣- encode cleaning by an agent. III Infectum is independently secured by JTM 2.13 and 9/3.
II.1b removes direct-object material (snow; weeds), unlike cleaning a location of m-marked material (PrS 19/57). The existing II Detransitive pest example parallels this removal construction.
Reflexive interpretation at 29/488 contrasts with attendants cleaning the youth at 29/487. It supports the inherited sich säubern possibility without proving a morphological Detransitive.

III manḍafwole in JTM 1.5/12–13 is ambiguous between Infectum-wa plus patient and Preterit-wa plus agent. Anterior German wording is insufficient to create a new Preterit-wa box; retain unresolved ledger classifications. JTM 2.11/8 securely supplies Infectum-wa.

Clean-state naḏ̣ifo/naḏ̣əfto/naḏ̣ife and tanḏ̣ifat/niḏ̣ofo are withheld as lexical adjectives/nouns. They remain documented in decisions and editorial questions, not published as newly established verbal forms.
Wind as a cleaning cause is a participant extension within III.1, already paralleled by grain becoming clean in I. Lexical contact does not by itself make a light-verb idiom.

Jan Beṯ-Şawoce round 2. All supplied English is project machine translation, not an edition translation; analyses and sense decisions rest on the Turoyo. Quoted English is copied verbatim and labelled as machine translation. Round-1 proposals are the baseline and are not repeated in this JSON.
Jan consistently distinguishes II mnaḏf- from III manḏəf-/manḏ̣əf-. Non-emphatic written ḏ is retained; it does not license changing the assigned root or normalizing source forms.

The II Infectum-wa box exists but remains empty after R1; mnaḏfiwo with az zabəqone fills it. III Infectum-wa is already established by R1 JTM 2.11/8, so Jan tokens fill a thin cell rather than establish it anew.

manḏ̣əfowalan at Jan 2.5/1530 is compared with manḏ̣əfolan at Jan 2.6/1773: both have the church as feminine theme and a first-person-plural cleaner, alongside matching səmowalan/ftəḥolan. This supplies a more constrained Preterit-wa candidate than R1's ambiguous -wo-le forms. The Jan proposal does not retroactively settle those R1 tokens.
III themes include church, bins, toilets, kiln and edible plants. These vary the cleaned object, not the lexical meaning. No new craft or religious cleaning sense is needed.

No new idiom is established: sweeping streets and cleaning utensils or plants are ordinary cleaning frames. R1 technical blossom loss and direct-object material removal get no independent Jan support here.
Can morphological evidence establish any naḏ̣ifo/naḏ̣əfto/naḏ̣ife adjective as a productive Part act.? None is admitted here solely by shape.
Are tanḏ̣ifat and niḏ̣ofo independently borrowed nouns or members of a native Infinitiv paradigm? No II Infinitiv box is added.
Which -wo-le analysis is intended at JTM 1.5/12 and /13? Their identical form does not resolve Infectum-wa versus Preterit-wa.
Does the feminine subject of 1/31 remain the insect species throughout? The supplied clause supports pest removal; an implicit dwelling would alter the semantic assignment.
At 62/195, is the omitted cleaned object the parents or the area under them? No example selected while this remains unresolved.

Confirm manḏ̣əfo-wa-lan at Jan 2.5/1530 as feminine theme plus -wa and first-person-plural agent, compared with manḏ̣əfo-lan at Jan 2.6/1773; the alternative beneficiary reading has not been silently erased.
Verify contracted manḏ̣afwo at Jan 2.10/2678 against III manḏ̣əf and the stated habitual toilet-cleaning context.
Nəḏfiwo dado at Jan 1.59/2829 lacks its dish antecedent in the supplied verse; confirm that referent before using it as an isolated example.

rationale: The German verb is säubern; the supplied 7/11 translation also reads säuberte sie mit Alkohol.
